_note: follow-up commit adds the function entry below
justification: Dev-tooling: upgrade the prior-art guard (PreToolUse Write|Edit hook) to also fire on EDITS that add a data-source signature (a new fetcher def, an HTTP/DB call, or an external data URL), not just net-new files. This closes the hole that let an ANEF fetcher be added to an existing file with zero duplication check. Adds a known-constraint registry cross-check and an audit log. No production code; fail-open.

pre_impl.existing_data: The v1 hook fired only on Write to a NEW file under watched dirs; it bailed immediately on Edit (tool_name != Write) and on existing files. It was already registered for Edit|Write in settings.json, but the code never handled Edit.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The guard was assumed to cover duplication generally, but adding a capability via Edit to an existing file (the ANEF case in intelligence_brief.py) bypassed it entirely. Verified by simulating that exact edit: v2 now returns exit 2 and surfaces app/api/environmental/anef/route.ts, lib/nsw-planning-portal.ts and services/portal_constraints.py.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Extends the existing hook in place (does not add a new hook). Adds: Edit handling, a data-source SIGNATURE regex gate (so ordinary edits stay silent), concern extraction from the added content, a KNOWN-constraint set, and a JSONL audit log of every block. Reuses the same git-grep search and scoring.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Pure local hook. Any exception (bad stdin, git failure, log write) falls through to sys.exit(0) — fail-open, never blocks legitimate work on a hook bug.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A — a Python PreToolUse hook, not application code. It reads the tool payload from stdin and writes a block message to stderr with exit 2.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a dev could add a duplicate data source by editing an existing file and the guard never ran. After: such an edit is blocked with the existing implementations listed, and the only bypass is an explicit prior-art-checked acknowledgement that is logged.

functions.name: tokens
functions.input: a string (filename, symbol name, URL or added code block) to extract concern keywords from
functions.output: a set of lower-cased keyword tokens of length four or more, with camelCase split and stop-words removed
functions.if_none: an input with no qualifying tokens returns an empty set, and the hook then exits zero without blocking

values: N/A - no regulatory values. The KNOWN set is a list of concern keywords (anef, riparian, flood, ...) that already have data sources in this repo, used to strengthen the block signal.
queries: N/A - the hook runs a read-only git grep over the repo; it adds no database or API query.

break_it.scenario: An ordinary logic edit with no data-source signature is made to a watched file
break_it.what_happens: if the hook fired on every edit it would block all normal work with false positives
break_it.repro: the capability-add branch returns early unless the SIGNATURE regex (requests/httpx/fetcher def/external URL/SQL) matches the added content
break_it.how: the SIGNATURE gate means edits without a new data source exit 0 silently; only data-source additions are searched

break_it.scenario: The added content adds a fetcher for a capability that already exists (the ANEF case)
break_it.what_happens: a duplicate data source gets created with no discovery, as happened with ANEF
break_it.repro: piping an Edit payload whose new_string contains def _anef_field + fetch_protection_overlay returns exit 2 and lists the existing anef route, portal lib and portal_constraints
break_it.how: Edit handling + the KNOWN-constraint cross-check + the git-grep candidates block the edit and surface the existing implementations to reuse

break_it.scenario: The hook itself errors on a malformed payload or a git failure
break_it.what_happens: a hook crash could block every Write/Edit and halt all work
break_it.repro: any exception path (json load, git grep subprocess, log write) is wrapped and falls through to exit 0
break_it.how: fail-open by design — every error path exits 0, so a hook bug degrades to no-guard, never to a hard block

post_merge.manual_verify: Re-run the simulated ANEF edit against .claude/hooks/prior-art-guard.py and confirm exit 2 + candidates. Confirm an ordinary edit (no requests/url/fetcher) to a services/ file exits 0. Check .claude/prior-art-decisions.log records the block. The heavier CI data-source registry/ratchet remains a follow-up.
